q: For the pattern 'aabaabaaa', what is the value of the prefix function at the last position, π[8]?
explain:
Up to position 7, the borders keep growing: π = 0 1 0 1 2 3 4 5. That is, 'aabaabaa' has border 'aabaa' (5).

q = 8, character 'a': try to extend the border of length 5 → P[5] = 'b' ≠ 'a'
fall back: k = π[4] = 2 → P[2] = 'b' ≠ 'a'
fall back: k = π[1] = 1 → P[1] = 'a' = 'a' → k = 2
π[8] = 2

Check: 'aabaabaaa' ends with 'aa' and begins with 'aa'. No longer border fits.

q: Using the KMP prefix function, what is the length of the shortest period of the string 'abcabcabcab'? (A period p means s[i] = s[i + p] for all valid i.)
explain:
s = abcabcabcab,  n = 11
longest border = 'abcabcab' (length 8), so π[10] = 8
shortest period = n − π[n−1] = 11 − 8 = 3   ('abc' repeated)

q: Which statements about the KMP algorithm are true?
options: Its matching phase makes at most 2n character comparisons on a text of length n
It needs to back up in the text after a mismatch
Its preprocessing depends only on the pattern
It reports overlapping occurrences if it continues from π[m−1] after a match
explain:
(A) holds: each comparison either advances the text index (at most n times) or decreases q (at most n times in total). (C) holds: π is computed from P alone. (D) holds: continuing from the longest border finds the next overlapping occurrence.

(B) is false. Never backing up in the text is exactly KMP's advantage, and it makes KMP usable on streaming input.
